$comment: Canonical library data. Edit this file (or ask Claude to), then run: python3 build.py. Each entry's `image` is a filename in library/images/. Vocabulary terms must come from the controlled lists in build.py, which validates them.

entries.title: Crafting Culture, Detroit
entries.brief: A studio portfolio built on scale and contrast. Massive grotesk display type stacked two lines on a white ground, set tight, with no colour at all in the interface. Below it an asymmetric grid of high-contrast editorial photography and 3D render work runs full bleed to the frame edge, so the imagery carries every bit of the colour.

entries.title: Outfit
entries.brief: A storefront that commits entirely to one colour. Saturated red floods the page while the wordmark sits enormous inside a centred light panel, grotesk and knocked out at display scale. A four-up product grid shot in black and white sits beneath, holding its own against the red field.

entries.title: Our Projects, Kim Kneipp
entries.brief: A quiet interiors portfolio on a warm putty ground, with an oversized elegant serif headline in soft grey-green. A hairline motif leads the eye down into a card grid of work, where muted archival-toned photography sits under small captions.

entries.title: Archiste
entries.brief: An architecture studio that lets one photograph do the work. A curved concrete interior fills the whole viewport, dimmed just enough to carry type, and the studio name sits across it in enormous lowercase grotesk. Everything else is small and quiet: a one-line thesis, a row of social marks, and a single white card floating at the lower right holding the only call to action.

entries.title: Axiom Research
entries.brief: A research institute rendered as an instrument panel. On near-black, a generative attractor is drawn in thousands of fine gold threads, filling the frame like a plotted trace. The name sits over it in large white grotesk, pushed to the lower right, while monospace labels report system state in the corners. The only colour is the gold of the curve.

entries.title: Creative Marketing Agency
entries.brief: A marketing site built on a single rendered object. A warm orange-to-brown gradient fills the page while a stack of translucent glass discs, iridescent at the edges, tumbles across the right two thirds. Copy sits low on the left in clean geometric sans, with the headline knocked out in white and a pill call to action beneath.

entries.title: PieterKoopt
entries.brief: A service for selling paintings, staged as an attic discovery. A gilt-framed Van Gogh hangs in a dim, dust-toned room among sheeted furniture, the whole scene graded olive and sepia. The headline runs in condensed caps with the second line dropping into italic serif, so the type turns at exactly the point the sentence does.

entries.title: Superly
entries.brief: A carbon offset product that uses colour as its index. A centred headline in soft geometric sans sits in generous white space, and beneath it a row of tall rounded tiles, each a different saturated field, names one project type over a simple line icon. The palette does the categorising, so the row reads before any of the labels do.

entries.title: Belarosa Chalet
entries.brief: An alpine hotel that holds itself very still. A wide letterspaced nav sits across the top, then the page splits: a deep green serif statement on the left in generous white space, one photograph of the lit chalet at dusk on the right. No overlap, no gradient, nothing decorative. The restraint is the luxury signal.
